QuestionStmt.S: If the lines $$\frac{3-x}{2} = \frac{5y-2}{3\lambda+1} = 5 - z$$ and $$\frac{x+2}{-1} = \frac{1-3y}{7} = \frac{4-z}{2\mu}$$ are at right angles, then $7\lambda - 10\mu =$

Solution.S:
First line: $\frac{3-x}{2} = \frac{5y-2}{3\lambda+1} = 5 - z$. Rewrite as $\frac{x-3}{-2} = \frac{y-2/5}{(3\lambda+1)/5} = \frac{z-5}{-1}$. Direction ratios: $(-2, \frac{3\lambda+1}{5}, -1)$. Multiply by 5: $(-10, 3\lambda+1, -5)$.

Second line: $\frac{x+2}{-1} = \frac{1-3y}{7} = \frac{4-z}{2\mu}$. Rewrite $1-3y = -3(y-1/3)$, so $\frac{x+2}{-1} = \frac{y-1/3}{-7/3} = \frac{z-4}{-2\mu}$. Direction ratios: $(-1, -7/3, -2\mu)$. Multiply by 3: $(-3, -7, -6\mu)$.

For perpendicular lines, dot product of direction ratios = 0:
$(-10)(-3) + (3\lambda+1)(-7) + (-5)(-6\mu) = 0$
$30 - 7(3\lambda+1) + 30\mu = 0$
$30 - 21\lambda - 7 + 30\mu = 0$
$23 - 21\lambda + 30\mu = 0$
$21\lambda - 30\mu = 23$.

Now $7\lambda - 10\mu = \frac{1}{3}(21\lambda - 30\mu) = \frac{23}{3}$.

Thus the correct option is B: $\frac{23}{3}$.
